clue.text: Reportedly far from excited with topless greeting in house of ill repute

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for being far from excited is heard, not spelt

parts.note: someone far from excited is bored

indicators.note: topless says the greeting loses its top letter

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A jaded visitor gives a half-hearted hello on arriving at a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' turns BORED into BORD, a sound-alike; 'topless' cuts the H from HELLO to leave ELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordello is a brothel, a house where prostitutes work, hence one of ill repute.

clue.text: School where every Tory of note starts

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A school whose pupils include every Tory worth mentioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the first letters of every, Tory, of and note. ETON is the famous English boarding school that has educated many Conservative prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: See 12
Fire a colleague from Belfast?

parts.note: Belfast is in Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
a mate is a workmate or colleague

explanation.surface: Sacking a workmate from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like dismissal from a job but means stir up or enliven.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone with enthusiasm is to animate them: both verbs mean enliven or inspire.

clue.text: See 19
Tracksuit perhaps fits uphill runner

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the word for fits is read from bottom to top

parts.note: strops are fits of temper
the Wear is a river in north-east England, and a river is a runner in crosswords

explanation.surface: A tracksuit is just the right gear for someone jogging up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uphill' means read from the bottom; 'runner' is a classic crossword word for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is an example of athletic clothing, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Nerves of steel? I think not!

definitions.meaning: having nerves of steel means being free of any fright
a British exclamation of firm refusal, like 'not likely!'

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that they have steely nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an absence of fright and, as slang, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Train's hour late, extremely annoying — the usual reason?

indicators.note: annoying here means troubling or disturbing, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely takes only the outer letters of the word late

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles that the train is an hour late, and asks if the usual excuse applies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoying' looks like a comment on the delay but is the anagram signal. Southern Rail is a train operator in south-east England notorious, around 2018, for delays and strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail operator is cheekily offered as the habitual cause of late trains, a whimsical definition by reputation.

clue.text: It's briefly about a particular case, gripped by disease

indicators.note: gripped by says the letters from the case of particular sit inside the word for disease

parts.note: pox is a disease

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so take the first and last letters of particular

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely says a particular case of disease is roughly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a medical case but means the outside of 'particular'.
explanation.definitionFit: Approx is the standard abbreviation of approximately, a longer word for roughly.

clue.text: God in fallen idol making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A god who has fallen from grace staging his return.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters NIDO run across 'fallen idol'; 'making a comeback' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Stars wonderful, though the first eclipsed in constellation

indicators.note: eclipsed means hidden from view, so the first letter of the word for wonderful is lost

parts.note: plum means excellent, as in a plum job
Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Stars look wonderful even when one is blotted out in a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first eclipsed' drops the P from PLUM, leaving LUM. 'Stars' feels astronomical, matching the surface, but means famous people.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminaries are celebrated, eminent people, just as stars are in showbiz.

clue.text: Man bandaging cuts, his wares often thorny?

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping round, so the word for man goes around the word for cuts

parts.note: feller is an informal word for a man, a fellow
to lower prices is to cut them

explanation.surface: A man dressing his wounds, perhaps from handling prickly goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' looks like wounds needing a bandage but means reduces, as prices are cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selling blooms often has roses on offer, and roses have thorns, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Social gathering in competition with divers at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party contest held among divers out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges WITH DIVERS. A whist drive is a British village-hall evening where players move from table to table at the card game whist.
explanation.definitionFit: A whist drive is a social event at which people compete at a card game, scoring across many rounds.

clue.text: See 22 down
Initially raking in money, half of this ancient city

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for money

parts.note: coin is money

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of raking
half of keeps the first two of the four letters of this

explanation.surface: A city of old, where one was raking in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raking in money' reads as a phrase about profit; here 'in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Corinth was a major city-state of ancient Greece, on the isthmus near Athens.

clue.text: Complex relationship ending in disaster, one in imbroglio

indicators.note: this in places the letters inside the word for imbroglio

parts.note: an imbroglio is a tangle, a confused situation

indicators.note: ending in points to the final letter of disaster

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A messy love affair that ends badly, with one person caught in the muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in' gives R, from 'disaster'; R and I go into TANGLE via the second 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A love triangle is a romantic tangle of three people, a fraught arrangement.

clue.text: Teacher regularly catching head turning, concentrate

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the alternate letters wrap the reversed headland
regularly takes every other letter of teacher, starting from the second
turning means the word for head is read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A teacher keeps catching a pupil turning round and tells them to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentrate' looks like an order but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract, as in vanilla essence.

clue.text: Unaware your challenge can't be completed

definitions.meaning: without any idea of what is going on
read literally as lacking the hint the solver tackles, so the puzzle cannot be finished

explanation.surface: A solver admits ignorance because the puzzle defeats them.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means ignorant, and also literally without a clue, the thing a crossword solver needs.

clue.text: Delusional activity, drink evil stuff in whisky with violin players

parts.note: cha is tea, a drink
sin is wrongdoing, evil
grain whisky is a kind of whisky
bows are what play a violin's strings

explanation.surface: A drunk downs a dodgy mix of whisky while fiddlers play on.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuing rainbows is an idiom for pursuing unrealistic dreams, an activity built on illusion.

clue.text: Old actress eating only cream cakes?

parts.note: what one eats is one's diet
cream cakes alone make for food that is rich

explanation.surface: A former film star whose meals consisted solely of cream cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts read together as 'diet rich', which describes eating nothing but cream cakes. Marlene Dietrich was a German-born star of 1930s Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a celebrated screen star of the twentieth century, long since dead.

clue.text: Painting is about to come up

indicators.note: about means around, so the word is wraps the word for come up

parts.note: to rise is to come up

explanation.surface: A picture is on the verge of being brought up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places RISE between the I and S of 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises is a famous 1889 work by Vincent van Gogh.

clue.text: Cool in deep space

explanation.surface: Something trendy, out among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is hippie slang for great, and literally describes something a long way off.

clue.text: 1970s' fashion, flaming dull clothes exciting people

indicators.note: clothes means dresses or wraps, so the word for dull goes round the word for flaming

parts.note: flat means dull, lifeless
flaming suggests fire, which is red
rousers are people who stir others up

explanation.surface: A garish, dull outfit worn by rabble-rousers in the seventies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, meaning wraps round, not garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell-bottomed trousers that widen below the knee were a signature look of the 1970s.

clue.text: Scenario unfolding on busy route, somewhere in the north-west Pacific

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: unfolding means opening out and developing, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A plot playing out along a crowded road, set in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolding' rearranges SCENARIO into CRONESIA. The M1 is a motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a region of small islands in the western Pacific, north of the equator.

clue.text: Sound wheel part

indicators.note: sound says the word for wheel is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to roll is to wheel along

explanation.surface: A wheel component in good working order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective, healthy, but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is an actor's part in a play or film.

clue.text: See 8
Wife hasn't provided wicked little pest

indicators.note: hasn't means lacks, so the letters for provided are taken out of wife

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: A husband complains his wife has failed to give him what he needs, the wicked pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes IF from WIFE, leaving WE.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle that damages grain and other crops.

clue.text: Most desperate youth retrospectively securing passes

indicators.note: securing means holding inside, so the reversed youth wraps the word for passes
retrospectively means looking back, so the word for youth is read backwards

parts.note: a teen is a youth
dies is a euphemism, passes away

explanation.surface: A young person, looking back, clinging to exam passes in desperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes' suggests exam results but means passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: The neediest are the poorest or most in want, the most desperate of all.
